messages:
Ana: heads-up — ACME reported repeated 429s and 200-400ms latency spikes yesterday evening for their Dedicated pool. They say they have a reserved pool sized for 500 rps but were being capped around 300. Customer timeline attached in their ticket.

Mike: can you paste the exact error they saw? 429 wording matters (reserved_pool_exhausted vs rate_limit_global).

Ana: customer pasted this from their client logs: 
```
{"error":"429","message":"rate_limit_exceeded: reserved_pool_exhausted","request_id":"req-7f3a"}
```

Sam: quick hypothesis — sounds like two-layer throttle: route-level quota or gateway token bucket hit before requests hit dedicated nodes. We had a config drift in that customer's route tag so some traffic was routed to shared tier when the reserved pool was momentarily full.

Priya: do we have metrics to prove fallback happened? I can take point with the account once we have root cause. :thumbsup:

Mike: checking metrics now. Prometheus query I used to look at fallback events: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_routing_fallback_total{pool="acme-dedicated"}[5m])) by (reason)
```
I see a spike between 2026-03-12T20:05 and 20:25 UTC matching customer times. Count ~420 fallbacks.

Sam: logs show gateway responded 429 with reason reserved_pool_exhausted then routed fallback to shared which then applied global rate-limiter. snippet: 
```
2026-03-12T20:07:14Z INFO gateway req=req-7f3a route=api.v1.generate pool=acme-dedicated reason=reserved_pool_exhausted -> fallback=shared
2026-03-12T20:07:14Z WARN gateway req=req-7f3a response=429 reason=global_rate_limit
```

Ana: oh — so the reserved pool hit a temporary cap and fallback path encountered global limits, causing the client to see 429s even though they expected dedicated capacity.

Priya: how did the reserved pool hit cap if the pool is sized for 500 rps and they saw ~300?

Mike: found the misconfig — the pool's capacity config had the correct GPU counts but the effective throughput_cap override for that tenant was accidentally set to 300 after an infra rollout. config excerpt:
```
# simplified pool config
pool: acme-dedicated
capacity_gpus: 4
throughput_cap_per_sec: 300  # <-- should be 500
route_tags: ["acme-prod"]
```
The comment from the infra deploy history shows a spurious change 2026-03-12 19:55 UTC.

Sam: that explains it. Two issues compounded: 1) throughput cap was lowered to 300, 2) when cap hit we fallback to shared which had much stricter global rate limits for that route. 3) client retry/backoff pattern was aggressive, causing token-bucket to drain faster.

Ana: repro steps for eng-runtime if needed: 
1) reproduce with curl using their header that pins route: 
```
curl -v -H "X-ACME-Route: acme-prod" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```
2) simultaneously run a 350 rps loader for 5min. You should see reserved pool token drops and fallback counters increment.

Mike: added a short-term mitigation: increased throughput_cap back to 550 for acme-dedicated and added a guard to prevent accidental rollback via CI. Also tweaked fallback policy to prefer queuing for 5s before spilling to shared for enterprise customers with SLA. 

Sam: recommend we also increase shared-route global bucket for this account while we phase in a proper rollback-proof config. Otherwise customers will see 429s when their pool briefly saturates.

Priya: noted — I'll tell ACME we found the misconfiguration and have (a) restored capacity, (b) changed fallback policy to queue for 5s, (c) temporary global-bucket increase for their route. Will share ETA for full audit. :white_check_mark:

RateBot: ALERT 2026-03-12T20:06Z — routing.fallback spike for pool=acme-dedicated count=420 severity=medium

Ana: additional recommendation for customers: educate on client-side jittered exponential backoff + rate-limit headers. We should publish a short KB showing expected behavior when a reserved pool saturates: fallback -> possible 429s if shared bucket is constrained.

Priya: ACME replied in ticket: "Thanks — can you also confirm we won't be billed for requests that hit shared?" I'll follow up with billing team after we finalize mitigation.

Mike: billing note: we only bill successful generation token usage. Failed 429s are not charged. Confirming with Billing Ops now.

Sam: action items: 
- Mike: revert cap and push CI guard (done).
- Sam: add telemetry dashboard for reserved_pool_fallback per-customer (in progress).
- Priya: communicate to ACME and confirm billing/no-charge for 429s.
- Ana: draft KB on reserved-pool behavior and recommended client-side backoff.

Ana: OK closing thread once Priya confirms with customer. Thanks everyone. :pray:
